title: Consistent Hashing
description: Understand consistent hashing and its use in distributed systems.

options.text: When a node is added to a consistent hash ring, all keys must be redistributed
options.explanation: Only keys in the range between the new node and its predecessor need to move — on average K/N keys (where K is total keys, N is total nodes). This is the key advantage over simple modular hashing.

options.text: Virtual nodes help solve the problem of uneven key distribution across physical nodes
options.explanation: Without virtual nodes, nodes may be unevenly spaced on the ring, causing hot spots. Virtual nodes (multiple points per physical node) ensure more uniform distribution — each physical node owns many small ranges instead of one large one.

options.text: Consistent hashing guarantees perfectly equal load distribution
options.explanation: Even with virtual nodes, consistent hashing only provides approximately equal distribution. Perfect equality would require dynamic rebalancing based on actual load, not just key count.

options.text: Consistent hashing is only used for cache distribution
options.explanation: Consistent hashing is used in many distributed systems: database sharding (DynamoDB, Cassandra), load balancing, distributed caches, CDNs, and distributed file systems.
